The *Rādhattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 541) is a canonical verse text situated within the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It records the past-life merits, spiritual lineage, and avadāna/apadāna narrative of the elder (thera) Rādha. On SuttaCentral, translations into five languages are indexed [SuttaCentral].

No separate critical studies or citations from secondary research were recovered in the present search corpus. However, machine analysis reveals significant textual connections across Pali literature. Computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 298 shared passages between this text and 57 other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. In particular, the opening sequence of verses (§§0.1/1.3–7.4) exhibits high mutual reuse with several other Apadāna poems, including the *Mahākoṭṭhikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 539), the *Uruveḷakassapattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 540), the *Dabbamallaputtattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 536), the *Nandātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 25), and the *Mogharājattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 542) [DharmaNexus]. Later verse sections (§§11.4–16.4) also recur in other poems in the collection, such as the *Vaṅgīsattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 546), *Sīvalittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 545), *Soṇātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 26), and *Paṭācārātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 20) [DharmaNexus]. Substantial segments are additionally cited or shared across Pali commentaries, most notably both parts of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Outside the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus aligns passages (such as §17.1–17.2) with Sanskrit avadāna literature, including Kṣemendra's *Sumāgadhāvadāna* and the *Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna* [DharmaNexus].
